entries.name: Dashmart
notes: Water does not reach the appropriate heat level in the south bathroom. The facility does not have a method for drying hands at the kitchen handwashing sink. Debris is still accumulated inside the reach-in coolers.

entries.name: Kung Fu Tea
notes: The ice machine in the back of the facility has a substantial buildup of debris. The tapioca boba is held at an improper hot temperature of 127 degrees. Wiping cloths used for cleaning are stored on top of countertops. The person in charge cannot demonstrate basic knowledge of foodborne illnesses, holding temperatures or required sanitizers. The three-compartment sink faucet is in disrepair and cannot completely shut off. There is an inadequate air gap underneath the three-compartment sink drain leading to the floor drain. The establishment does not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees are not in possession of a valid food handler card. Food temperature-measuring devices are not provided or readily accessible. The facility lacks a chlorine testing kit to measure the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solution. The facility does not provide a designated area for employees to eat or drink. An employee’s drink is stored directly above the ice machine. No chlorine solution is being utilized to adequately achieve sanitization. The facility was using a Clorox multi-surface disinfectant that is explicitly not approved for food contact surfaces. An employee is wearing an unapproved watch and bracelets while preparing beverages. The facility is operating with an expired permit.

headline: Two businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: 999 Seafood Supermarket
notes: The person in charge was unable to demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention and other requirements of the food code and local ordinances. The person in charge was unable to provide records of training or certification for the food employees. Frozen raw fish was improperly thawed by being completely submerged in standing water inside a three-compartment sink. Heavy amounts of wastewater buildup were observed on the raw meat and seafood floor. Wastewater was being tracked through the facility and was unable to reach the floor drains. Nonfunctional and dirty items that are no longer used, such as refrigerators, tanks, maintenance equipment, kitchen supplies, scales and tables, were found throughout the entire facility and outdoor area. Critical parts of the premises, including the floors, ceilings and physical facilities, were severely damaged and in need of repair. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. There was no testing kit or other device available to measure the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solution. A meat scale at the meat and seafood counter was severely soiled with food residue, meat residue and insect buildup. Raw fish in the seafood walk-in freezer was contacting an unapproved surface by being stored uncovered inside a shopping cart left against a wall. Raw chicken in the raw meat walk-in cooler was stored improperly above pork and beef. The packaging of the raw chicken was bloody and dripping. Spoiled seafood products in a state of decay were not separated from safe products and shared the same ice and display case as wholesome products. Drain pipes and PVC plumbing for three sinks, condensers and large tanks throughout the meat and seafood areas were not maintained in good repair and had severe malfunctions causing major leaks. An inadequate air gap was observed at the floor drain under the three-compartment sink. The food establishment did not have temperature logs available for any species of raw meat and seafood being stored, thawed or cooled. Holes and gaps varying in size from one-half inch to three inches were observed along the ceiling and floors in the meat and seafood area. An electrocution insect control device was installed directly over a food preparation area at the meat and seafood wrapping station. The facility showed severe signs of an active pest infestation and failed to prevent further growth or harborage of rodents. Bait stations in the rear stockroom were not covered or tamper-resistant, leaving the toxic bait inside the trap exposed. An employee at the meat and seafood counter failed to change single-use gloves when switching between handling raw proteins and filling ice. Raw fish in the walk-in freezer was stored improperly less than six inches off the floor. A food employee did not wash their hands when required after drinking from a bottle before handling food items. A food employee was observed handling different raw animal species without washing their hands. Light bulbs throughout the facility stockrooms and walk-in coolers lacked protective shielding or covers to make them shatter-resistant. Multiple light bulbs were burned out throughout the meat and seafood areas and coolers, resulting in an inadequate amount of lighting. Food-contact surfaces, including cutting boards, cleavers, knives, scoops and meat display trays, were heavily soiled with food debris and unknown residues. The facility did not provide a designated area for employees to eat, drink, or use tobacco products. The facility did not provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the storage of employee clothing or personal belongings. Multiple display trays in the meat display case were not maintained in good repair and had holes and breaks. Butcher cutting boards in the meat department prep area had deep scratches and scoring that limited the ability to effectively clean and sanitize them. Handwashing fixtures in the raw meat service area were severely soiled with a buildup of soil residues. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts had debris buildup inside the ambient coolers, walk-in coolers and vent covers over the food production area in the raw meat and seafood section. Working containers taken from bulk supplies, including wiping cloth buckets and spray bottles allegedly containing chlorine, degreaser and unknown chemical solutions, were not properly labeled.

entries.name: 999 Seafood Supermarket
notes: Mice droppings were found under the service counter storage racks, on wood shelving and on storage area shelving. Duck marinade was stored in the walk-in cooler with no date-mark indicators or identification labels. Corn starch was stored in an unapproved non-NSF container. Multiple bulk food containers had an accumulation of crusted soil buildup. The person in charge was unable to demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention and local food regulations. Food employees did not have a valid food handler card and lacked approved training records. An open container of tofu was left uncovered and unprotected from contamination inside a reach-in cooler. The testing kit used to measure the concentration of chemical sanitizing solutions had expired as of September 1, 2025. A food employee kept an unapproved bottled water drink on a kitchen food storage rack. The front service handwash station lacked sufficient hot water and only reached a temperature of 70 degrees. A buildup of debris and residue was observed on the walls and floors in the food preparation areas. The walls above the sink at the kitchen washing station were made of RPC and were not smooth or easily cleanable.

entries.name: Los Tacos Del Rey
notes: The chlorine sanitizing solution in the front-end wiping cloth bucket and the three-compartment sink tested at an inadequate concentration of 0 to 25 PPM. Multiple reach-in coolers throughout the kitchen contained ready-to-eat items such as salsas, aguas, sliced cheeses and cooked meats with no required date markings or expiration dates. The floor drain directly under the three-compartment sink lacked an adequate air gap. Bulk dry food storage containers in the rear kitchen were missing common name labels after being removed from their original packaging. Multiple cartons of raw shelled eggs in the rear standing cooler were stored improperly on a grate directly over bulk unprotected cilantro. The facility lacked accessible food temperature-measuring devices and multiple cold-holding units were missing required ambient thermometers. No lockers or suitable storage facilities were provided for employee clothing and personal belongings. Handwashing sinks located in the restrooms and at the kitchen make line station were missing visible handwashing signs. Stainless steel surfaces in and around the deep fryer on the make line showed a heavy accumulation of grease and debris. The establishment failed to maintain required temperature logs for storing, thawing or cooling items like cooked meats, salsas, chopped veggies, beans, rice and aguas.

entries.name: Royal Hyderabad
notes: The interior and exterior of the warewashing machine had a substantial buildup of food debris. Frozen chicken was improperly thawing at room temperature on a milk crate in the kitchen prep area. Wiping cloths were stored improperly on top of a food-contact surface. Multiple ready-to-eat items in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler lacked required date markings or expiration dates, including yellow curry paste, cooked chicken red sauce, yogurt and strawberry milk. The person in charge failed to demonstrate basic knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, reportable illnesses and required holding or reheating temperatures. The establishment could not provide valid food handler cards or training records for its employees. An open bag of dried basil and 10 containers of unknown spices were left uncovered in the storage area. Multiple TCS foods in the prep top coolers were measured at unsafe temperatures above 41 degrees, including unknown green paste, cooked cold potatoes, chili sauce, green cooked curry chicken and red curry cooked chicken. Condensation and ice from leaking water lines were dripping onto shrimp and other unknown food items stored directly on the walk-in freezer floor. Several containers of unknown sauces and food items were left uncovered inside the walk-in cooler. Approved hand drying provisions were missing from both the kitchen handwash station and the employee restroom. The facility lacked required temperature logs for cooked, hot-held or cold-held meats and seafood, as well as calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

headline: Three businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Tanoan Country Club
notes: Numerous rodent droppings were found throughout the property. A rodent nest with a dead mouse was found inside the nesting material. Water leaked profusely from the top of the ice machine. Organic growth was present on the ice machine panels and piping. A plastic cutting surface had deep scratches and scoring. Service counter shelving was improperly installed and had unsealed gaps. Rodent droppings were located on and under the service counter shelving. The floor drain lacked an adequate plumbing air gap. An untreated wood surface had spillage and droppings present. Outside doors were not tight-fitting and showed large gaps. A screen door was damaged, allowing potential pest entry. The swamp cooler and electrical panel box had unsealed openings into the structure. Dirt and debris built up on floors and walls behind equipment. Walls and wall-floor junctures had numerous holes and crevices.

entries.name: Bamboo
notes: The warewashing machine had 0 ppm chlorine sanitizer concentration. Food containers and cooking utensils had heavy debris and grease buildup. Employees used an unapproved Raid pesticide spray inside the kitchen. Raw meat was thawed improperly in a sink basin without running water. Soap splattered onto the raw meat during dishwashing. An active cockroach infestation was observed throughout the facility. Live cockroaches crawled directly on onions and carrots meant for service. Cockroaches were found on the deli slicer and inside utensil containers. One pest trap contained an estimated total of over 100 cockroaches. Multiple prepared sauces and teas lacked required date markings. Food container lids were broken with visible cracks and holes. The ice machine door was missing and was replaced with a taped plastic sheet. Plastic cutting boards had deep scratches and score marks. Outdoor waste bins lacked tight-fitting lids and were overfilled. The person in charge failed to demonstrate food-safety knowledge. The handwashing plumbing leaked liquid waste onto the floor. The mop sink and handwashing sink lacked plumbing air gaps. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. Kitchen ventilation ducts had a heavy buildup of debris. Numerous food containers and storage bags were unlabeled. Outside doors were not tight-fitting and let light through the edges. The outdoor dumpster area had accumulated grease and waste. Cooked garlic and noodles were held at unsafe temperatures. Bags of tea were stored directly on the floor. Open employee drinks were stored directly on the food prep line. Employee jackets and shoes were stored on top of single-use food packaging. The chlorine sanitizer concentration exceeded 100 ppm. An employee prepared open food without wearing a hair restraint. The facility operated with an expired permit. An employee killed a cockroach with their bare hand and handled food surfaces without washing. Floors and walls throughout the kitchen had severe debris accumulation. The menu lacked a proper consumer advisory warning. Serving scoops were stored with handles directly touching the food. Clean food containers were wet-stacked instead of air drying. Walls and ceilings had numerous gaps, holes and cracks. An indoor wall attachment was made of porous untreated wood.

entries.name: Dragonhorn Tavern
notes: Brown and yellow buildup was found inside the ice machine bin. Chemical spray bottles lacked labels identifying their contents. Open hot dogs and Colby cheese exceeded the seven-day storage limit. Floor drains under the ice machine and bar sink lacked the required plumbing air gaps. Food employees did not have valid food handler cards. The back door was not tight-fitting and let light through the edges. Ribbon-cut fries were stored directly on the floor of the walk-in cooler. The bar’s handwashing sink lacked a handwashing reminder sign. Multiple ceiling tiles were missing throughout the building. Required temperature logs were unavailable for stored food items.

entries.name: Cracker Barrel
notes: The wall sanitizer dispenser above the three-compartment sink was empty. A pan of cream gravy on the steam table was held at an unsafe temperature. Shredded potatoes in the walk-in cooler had an incorrect 14-day use-by date. The temperature gauge on the mechanical warewashing machine was broken. Uncooked country ham was stored directly next to ready-to-eat desserts and food. An employee kept an open energy drink can next to customer food items. Hot water in the employee restrooms failed to reach the required temperature. Dirt and debris built up on the floors beneath the kitchen line equipment. Floor debris accumulated in the warewashing area near the dish machine. Broken floor tiles caused stagnant water to pool.

entries.name: Days Inn & Suites
notes: The chlorine sanitizing solution in a kitchen wiping-cloth container measured only 25 ppm. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or accessible. There was no testing kit to measure chemical sanitizer concentrations. Ambient air thermometers were completely missing from two upright coolers and a drop-in freezer. The facility operated with an expired permit. A soiled mop was stored directly on the floor while not in use. The facility lacked required calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Filiberto’s
notes: The can opener, produce dicer and ice machine had dried food debris and soil buildup. Multiple containers of chopped vegetables, cooked meats, beans, salsas and cheeses lacked date markings. The spray nozzle and faucet on the three-compartment sink leaked significantly. The person in charge could not provide the required food handler cards for employees. Cooked meats, cheeses, rellenos and chopped vegetables were stored uncovered inside the coolers. Physical and liquid waste pooled inside the outdoor trash receptacle enclosure. Fajita vegetables, asada, sliced cheese, green salsa and pico de gallo were held at unsafe temperatures. The facility lacked a designated area for employee dining. No lockers or designated storage facilities were provided for employee clothing and personal items. An employee chopped produce after sweeping and handling non-ready-to-eat foods without washing their hands. The grill top and deep fryer were heavily soiled with grease and food residue.

entries.name: La Carreta Hotdogs & Tacos
notes: WD40 and bug spray were stored directly on and under a kitchen prep table. Chopped green chile, horchata, onions and tomatoes lacked required date markings. The kitchen area completely lacked a handwashing sink. The three-compartment sink lacked an adequate backflow air gap. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. A container of horchata was stored uncovered inside a reach-in cooler. Temperature-measuring devices for thin foods were not provided. No chlorine test strips were available to measure sanitizer concentrations. The facility operated with an expired permit. No health grade sticker was displayed at the facility. The food permit was not posted on the premises. The grease trap could not be located or accessed due to obstructions. The ceiling had holes, missing tiles, and peeling paint and tape. An electrical plug was missing its protective plate. Required temperature logs for hot holding, cold holding, and cooling were unavailable. The facility lacked calibration logs for thermometers.

entries.name: Royal Hyderabad
notes: The facility has been upgraded from closure to unsatisfactory and needs to be inspected again within 5 business days.

entries.name: Little Anita’s
notes: Chlorine sanitizer levels in the dishwasher and sanitizer buckets measured 0 ppm. Toxic grill cleaner was stored directly next to tortillas and ready-to-eat food. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. Sour cream, guacamole, tomatoes, meat and potatoes were held at unsafe temperatures in the prep cooler. The walk-in cooler failed to maintain safe temperatures for cooked beef, chicken, rice and chili. The walk-in freezer failed to keep raw chicken and vegetables frozen. Required food thermometers were unavailable or inaccessible near the prep cooler. The facility lacked a chemical test kit to measure sanitizer concentrations. No paper towels or approved hand drying methods were provided at the handwashing sinks. The restroom handwashing sink lacked a required reminder sign. An employee prepared and handled avocados without wearing a hair restraint. An employee stored an open Gatorade drink inside the walk-in freezer. Dirt and debris built up on the floors, walls and ceiling tiles in the kitchen. A food scoop was stored with its handle directly touching ready-to-eat beef and potatoes. Four kitchen knives were stored improperly in the gap between the prep cooler and the steam table. Ceramic floor tiles in the service area were broken and difficult to clean.

entries.name: Sergio’s Bakery
notes: The quaternary ammonium sanitizer in a wiping-cloth bucket measured 0 ppm. Significant debris built up inside the ice machine. Debris accumulated on the can opener blade. Dressings, soft cheeses, cakes and cannoli fillings lacked required date markings. Some stored food items exceeded the seven-day holding limit. Outdoor waste bins were overflowing with their lids left completely open. The person in charge failed to demonstrate necessary food safety knowledge. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. Ventilation intake and exhaust air ducts had a heavy accumulation of debris. The toilet room lacked a tight-fitting, self-closing door. Outside doors were not tight-fitting and let light through the edges. Significant waste and debris built up around the outdoor dumpsters and grease containers. The facility failed to provide a designated dining area for employees. The facility lacked lockers for employee belongings. The service station handwashing sink lacked an approved hand-drying method. Cleaning implements and wiping cloths were stored inside a handwashing sink. Employees prepared and handled open food items without the required hair restraints. Food employees failed to wash their hands when switching tasks or changing gloves. No written allergen warnings were provided for unpackaged food items. Heavy debris and organic growth built up on the walk-in cooler shelving. Black organic growth covered the plastic wrap of a wheel of cheese. The facility lacked required daily temperature logs for its food products. No calibration logs were maintained for the facility’s thermometers.

entries.name: Sergio’s Bakery
notes: The person in charge failed to demonstrate necessary food safety knowledge. The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards. The outdoor dumpster and grease container area had significant debris buildup. Various cakes in the display case were held at unsafe temperatures up to 58 degrees. Walls and ceilings had numerous holes, gaps, cracks and missing tiles. Food scoops were stored improperly, with handles touching the dry goods. An ice scoop was stored on top of a soiled container. Bakery to-go containers were stored directly on the floor. Equipment handles, shelving and walk-in cooler surfaces had heavy debris and organic growth. Living flies were observed landing inside an open container of mascarpone cheese. Piping and faucets at the three-compartment sink leaked wastewater. The bakery sink area lacked an adequate plumbing air gap. The facility lacked required temperature logs and thermometer calibration logs. No written allergen warnings were provided for unpackaged food items. Packaged bagels, breads and pastries lacked required labels. Outside doors were propped open and were not tight-fitting. Living flies were present in the bakery with no pest control methods in place. Numerous baked foods were stored improperly outdoors. Bags of flour and multiple food fillings were stored directly on the floor. Single-use containers were improperly reused to store soaking raisins. Employees failed to wash their hands when changing gloves or touching their bodies and hair. The owner contaminated their hands while washing by touching a dirty faucet and paper towel dispenser. Severe debris and buildup accumulated on walls and floors throughout the facility. The quaternary ammonium sanitizer bucket measured 0 ppm. Numerous baking pans had significant burnt-on or caked-on grease. Measuring cups, the ice machine and general bakery equipment had heavy soil buildup. The handwashing sink was blocked with personal beverage lids and a pastry piping bag. Ventilation ducts throughout the bakery and warewashing area had heavy debris buildup. The toilet room door was propped open and was not self-closing. An employee wore unapproved wrist jewelry while handling open food. A food employee prepared baked goods without a proper hair restraint.

entries.name: Sheraton Albuquerque Airport Hotel
notes: A deli slicer and a can opener had a buildup of food debris between uses. Cooked shredded chicken in the walk-in cooler completely lacked the required date markings. The cold water faucet line at the three-compartment sink leaked. Several kitchen floor drains lacked the required plumbing air gaps. Kitchen hood vents and air ducts had an accumulation of debris. Outside doors were not tight-fitting and let light through the edges. Cooked shredded chicken in the walk-in cooler was held at an unsafe temperature of 53 degrees. Red and green chile sauces were stored uncovered inside the walk-in cooler. An employee wore an unapproved wristwatch while working on the cook line. A metal food scoop handle was in direct contact with white flour inside a bulk storage container.

entries.name: Vic’s Daily Cafe
notes: Ibuprofen medication was improperly stored on a kitchen line shelf above the prep cooler. The facility maintained inadequate procedures to effectively control pests. Three dead rodents and one dead cockroach accumulated in traps under the water heater. An employee touched an order ticket with gloves soiled from cracking raw eggs. The backflow prevention device at the service sink faucet was damaged and was leaking. The back screen door was not tight-fitting and let light through the top and bottom edges. Ice cubes were found draining inside the server area handwashing sink. An employee put on new gloves without washing their hands in between changes.

headline: Twelve businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: 999 Seafood Supermarket
notes: Minimal rodent droppings remained present within the grocery aisles. A rodent dropping was observed directly on the bulk rice bags. Rodent droppings were present in the back stock storage area for dry goods. Droppings accumulated on boxes of chopsticks and trash bags. Significant debris accumulation was noted throughout the aisle shelving.

entries.name: Amadeo’s Pizza & Subs
notes: The can opener, bulk storage tubs and deli slicer were soiled with dried food residue. A five-gallon working bucket of bleach sanitizer water lacked a label identifying its contents. The facility had an active cockroach infestation that failed to be controlled. The person in charge failed to demonstrate basic food safety knowledge regarding the six reportable illnesses. The three-compartment sink faucet was missing its handle and could not be turned on and off properly. The grease trap leaked grease and liquid waste sludge onto the kitchen floor. Kitchen ventilation intake and exhaust air ducts had an accumulation of debris. Raw shell eggs were stored directly above ready-to-eat romaine lettuce inside the walk-in cooler. Ambient thermometers were missing or inaccessible in multiple cold-holding units. The facility was found operating with an expired permit. Clean single-use cups, lids, and containers were stored directly on the floor. Cockroaches were using the floor-stored single-use containers as a harborage area. A vegetable oil container was improperly reused to store a bulk powdered ingredient. Floor and wall juncture coving was absorbent, damaged and difficult to clean. The building had missing floor tiles, damaged wall attachments and multiple unsealed holes throughout. Required temperature logs were unavailable for the stored food products.

entries.name: Einstein Bros. Bagels
notes: Substantial debris built up inside the back ice machine. Plastic cutting boards provided unsafe and non-smooth food contact surfaces. The three-compartment sink faucet could not shut off completely. The soda machine leaked a substantial amount of water onto the floor. Kitchen floor drains had a buildup of debris. Food employees lacked required food handler cards. Kitchen ventilation intake and exhaust ducts had a buildup of debris. A working container of flour or corn meal lacked a common name label. Synthetic wood shelving inside storage cabinets was damaged and unsealed. The men’s restroom was out of order because the toilet failed to flush. No chemical test kit was available to measure sanitizer concentrations. An employee wore unapproved bracelets while preparing breakfast sandwiches. The facility operated with an expired permit and an unverified business registration. No food permit was conspicuously posted on the premises. The three-compartment sink lacked cold water and only provided hot water at 140 degrees. Quat sanitizer was improperly mixed with only hot water due to the missing cold water. Employees completely failed to wash their hands during the entire inspection. Cashiers prepared drinks and line cooks donned gloves without washing their hands. Line cooks cracked raw eggs and then handled sandwiches without washing hands. Debris built up inside cabinets, under equipment and on kitchen shelving.

entries.name: Hilton Garden Inn
notes: An extreme buildup of black organic matter was observed inside the kitchen ice machine. Chopped green chile, sliced tomatoes and cut squash exceeded the seven-day storage limit. Several floor drains located throughout the kitchen lacked an adequate plumbing air gap. Sliced tomatoes, chopped green chile and Greek yogurt were held at unsafe cold-holding temperatures. The upright cooler near the cook line was insufficient and failed to maintain proper temperatures. The facility lacked a chemical testing kit or device to measure sanitizer concentrations. The handwashing sink located in the bar area lacked a required handwashing reminder sign. A back-of-house handwashing station was blocked and rendered inaccessible by a mop bucket. An employee wore unapproved items of jewelry while actively preparing consumer food. A soiled mop was stored improperly by being left directly on the floor while not in use.

entries.name: Hot Dog Man
notes: Chlorine sanitizer in a spray bottle and wiping cloth container measured 0 ppm. The mobile unit lacked a testing kit to measure chemical sanitizer concentrations. No hand soap was available at the handwashing station. The handwashing sink lacked an approved hand-drying method. The handwashing sink lacked a required handwashing reminder sign. The handwashing sink was used improperly to store hand tools and discard drinks. An employee did not wash hands when switching tasks and donning a new glove. An employee used a soiled cloth and dirty water to wash hands without cleanser. A plastic working spray bottle containing an unknown chemical lacked a label. A food handler was observed working with unkempt fingernails. An employee prepared food inside the unit without a proper hair restraint.

entries.name: Kobe Pho
notes: The deli slicer in the rear kitchen was soiled with food debris. Various broths, chopped vegetables, prepared meats and house-made sauces lacked required date markings. The person in charge was unable to provide required employee food handler cards. Ventilation intake and exhaust air ducts above the prep area had a buildup of debris. Chopped fruit, broth and sliced onions were held at unsafe temperatures inside the reach-in cooler. Ambient thermometers were missing or inaccessible in multiple cold-holding units. The facility failed to provide a designated area for employee dining. No lockers or suitable storage facilities were provided for employee clothing and personal items. Front and rear kitchen handwashing sinks were blocked by kitchen equipment and soiled utensils sitting inside the basins. Dirt and debris built up on kitchen floors and walls, especially underneath equipment. Clean single-use deli cups were stored improperly directly on the floor at the server station. Fryers, the grill top, reach-in coolers and storage shelving were soiled with grease and food debris. Required temperature logs were unavailable for hot and cold temperature-controlled foods.

entries.name: SpringHill Suites
notes: The quaternary ammonium sanitizer in the food prep area measured 0 ppm. The required chemical sanitizer solution was not prepped for the day. Sliced ham and sliced cheese inside the upright cooler lacked required date markings. The person in charge failed to demonstrate necessary food safety knowledge. The floor drain near the warewash machine was in disrepair and missing a strainer. The floor drain near the warewash machine lacked an adequate backflow air gap. Food portioning containers for nuts and coconut flakes in the self-serve area lacked common name labels. A food employee prepared food for the self-serve area without a proper hair restraint. An employee failed to wash their hands when switching tasks and donning new gloves. The facility lacked required calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: The Paleta Bar
notes: Dried food and soil debris accumulated on a can opener blade in the back prep area. A working spray bottle containing an unknown chemical lacked an identifying label. Working containers holding spices and an unknown white food product completely lacked required common name labels. Butter, cotija cheese, diced honeydew and diced cantaloupe were held at unsafe cold-holding temperatures. Required food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. The facility lacked a functional sanitizer testing kit, and its available test strips were expired. The back handwashing sink in the kitchen prep area lacked an approved method for hand drying. One front handwashing sink was blocked by a towel left inside the basin. Another front handwashing sink was completely blocked by a broom, dustpan and squeegee. Chemical sanitizer in a chlorine wiping cloth bucket exceeded the maximum limit at 200 ppm. An employee wore an unapproved watch while actively handling open food items. A food employee prepared open food items in the kitchen without a proper hair restraint. A soiled mop was stored improperly by being left directly on the floor while not in use. Buildup and debris accumulated on the floors and walls across the kitchen prep area. The facility failed to provide written allergen warnings for its unpackaged food items. Food scoops and cups were stored with handles directly touching the food products. Food and soil debris built up inside a front floor drain and on the three-compartment sink sprayer. The sides of the ice cream machines had a noticeable accumulation of soil residue. Organic growth was found inside a non-working cooler unit located behind the front counter. The wall next to the front handwashing sink was in disrepair with a golf ball-sized hole. The establishment completely lacked required temperature logs for its stored food products. No calibration logs were maintained for the facility’s temperature-measuring devices.

headline: Eight businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Amadeo’s Pizza & Subs
notes: Facility has been upgraded to unsatisfactory following submission of photographic evidence and in-person walk-through of corrected violations by the Environmental Health Department.

entries.name: Empire Board Game Library
notes: Black organic matter built up on the interior of the back-of-house ice machine. The floor drain under the three-compartment sink lacked an adequate backflow air gap. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees completely lacked required food handler cards. The toilet room lacked a tight-fitting, self-closing door or was left propped open. Sliced turkey, pre-cooked chicken and pre-cooked bacon were held at unsafe cold temperatures. The facility lacked a current testing kit to measure chemical sanitizer concentrations. No food thermometer was available to check accuracy at the sandwich-making station. An employee wore an unapproved wristwatch while actively handling food. The facility was found operating with an expired permit. A soiled mop was stored improperly directly inside a mop bucket instead of being hung to dry. Required temperature logs were unavailable for stored food products. The facility completely lacked calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Freddy’s
notes: Quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution on the main cook line and behind the front counter measured 0 ppm. The interior of the ice machine bin had a substantial organic buildup. The can opener blade was soiled with a buildup of food and soil debris. Floor drains were in disrepair due to missing protective mesh or dome covers. Floor drains at the drive-thru and the back door lacked adequate backflow air gaps. A working container holding seasoning lacked a required common name label. Sautéed onions, sautéed mushrooms, relish, sliced tomatoes, diced onions, diced tomatoes and shredded lettuce were held at unsafe cold temperatures. The facility failed to provide a designated area for employee dining or tobacco use. Employee water bottles were stored inside the walk-in cooler directly above facility food items. Handwashing cleanser was unavailable at the hand sinks by the manager’s office and behind the front counter. The handwashing sink by the warewashing area lacked an approved hand-drying method. A soiled mop was stored improperly by being left directly on the floor while not in use. Buildup and debris accumulated on the kitchen floors and walls under and behind equipment, tables and shelving. Food service pans were stacked wet instead of being allowed to air dry. Nonfood contact surfaces on fryers, coolers, the warewashing spray nozzle, TV screens, walk-in fan shrouds and soda machine cabinets had a buildup of food and soil debris.

entries.name: Homewood Suites
notes: Brown organic matter built up near the ice chute of the kitchen ice machine. An inadequate plumbing air gap was observed near the warewash machine. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees completely lacked required food handler cards. A metal can of sliced jalapeños was dented and compromised. The handwashing sink on the kitchen south wall lacked an approved hand-drying method. A mop bucket blocked access to the kitchen south wall handwashing sink. Required temperature logs were unavailable for hot and cold stored foods. The facility lacked calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Icon Cinema
notes: The ice cream well sink drain pipe lacked an adequate backflow air gap. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Unsealed wood shelf organizers at the front register and popcorn areas provided porous, absorbent surfaces. Hot dogs and containers of drained sliced jalapeños were held at unsafe cold temperatures. The upright cooler in the warewashing area failed to maintain required cold-holding temperatures. Containers of diced green chile developed an unsafe white film on top. Cleaned wood shelf organizers were stored improperly, less than six inches above the floor.

headline: Five businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Bamboo
notes: Live cockroaches were present in the warewashing area. Live cockroaches were found in the dining room service area. Numerous dead cockroaches had accumulated inside the facility. Walls, shelving and the sides of equipment had a buildup of debris. The interior of slicing equipment still had debris accumulation. Holes, gaps, cracks and crevices were noted throughout the facility.

entries.name: Eat My Thai Cuisine
notes: Plates, bowls, knives, a produce slicer and the ice machine deflector in clean storage were soiled with food residue. More than 20 dead cockroaches had accumulated throughout the facility. Ready-to-eat TCS foods in all cold-holding units lacked required date markings. A food employee touched chopped vegetables and prepared meats on the cook line with bare hands. The person in charge failed to demonstrate adequate food-safety knowledge. Multiple plumbing faucets and drain pipes were leaking and in disrepair. Floor drains under the three-compartment sink and dishwashing machine lacked proper air gaps. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Interior ventilation intake and exhaust air ducts had substantial debris buildup. Batter, sliced vegetables, soups and pot stickers were stored uncovered in coolers. Broken utensils, unused dishes and nonfunctional kitchen equipment accumulated on the premises. Chopped onions, pot stickers, green onions, sliced carrots, chicken chunks and sliced cucumbers were held at unsafe temperatures. Bulk cases of rice, curry paste and sauces were stored directly on the floor. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or accessible. No hand soap was available at the boiler room sink, and a heavily watered-down soap mixture was used at the make line sink. Both kitchen handwashing sinks were blocked and inaccessible due to stored supplies and equipment. A food employee peeled shrimp in the kitchen without wearing proper hair restraints. Kitchen floors, walls and the cook line had a heavy accumulation of grease, debris and food residues. The facility failed to maintain any required temperature logs for stored food products.

entries.name: KFC
notes: All quaternary ammonium sanitizer buckets were empty despite the store being open for business. Soda machine nozzles in the dining room had a buildup of syrup and debris. Clean food service pans in the kitchen were soiled with dried food and soil debris. Two to four dozen dead cockroaches accumulated in the kitchen and dining areas. Coleslaw and pot pies in the walk-in cooler lacked required date markings. Floor drains under the front counter and near the drive-thru window lacked proper air gaps. The eastern outer front doors had small holes at the bottom that let light inside. No sanitizer testing kit was available in the facility. The facility did not provide a designated area for employee dining or tobacco use. A soiled mop was stored improperly directly on the floor. Substantial debris built up on kitchen and dining room floors and walls under shelving and equipment. Food service pans were stacked wet in the warewashing area instead of being air dried. The back plates of the soda machines had heavy syrup and debris buildup. The sides and backs of the fryers had substantial grease buildup. Dining room tables and chairs had an accumulation of dried food and soil debris. The sides of the three-compartment sink had heavy debris buildup. Wax paper holders on the main line had heavy debris buildup. Gas, water and electric pipes in the kitchen had substantial grease buildup.

entries.name: Kokio Korean Fried Chicken
notes: Working spray bottles containing sanitizer and coconut oil lacked required identifying labels. Prepared potatoes, kimchi, sliced cabbage and sliced onions lacked required date markings. The facility did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not have valid food handler cards. Kitchen containers holding flour and bulk spices lacked required common name labels. Cardboard used to cover kitchen shelving was torn, damaged, absorbent and not smooth. A stock pot of teriyaki sauce was stored improperly directly on the kitchen floor. The establishment failed to provide a designated area for employee dining. Handwashing cleanser was unavailable at the kitchen handwashing sink. The kitchen handwashing sink was blocked by a large pot of teriyaki sauce. Required temperature-measuring devices were missing from the cold-holding units, reach-in floor freezers and standing freezer. The facility was found operating with an expired permit. The food establishment permit was not conspicuously posted inside the facility. Required temperature logs were unavailable for stored and received TCS food items. The establishment completely lacked calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Which Wich
notes: Severe debris and grease built up on a conveyor-style toaster oven. Dried food debris accumulated on a prep table can opener blade. A restroom toilet was in disrepair and unable to flush. A three-compartment sink sprayer nozzle leaked, causing standing water to seep into the dining area walkway. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees completely lacked required food handler cards. Metal wire shelves inside the walk-in cooler were rusty and dirty. Sliced tomatoes, cucumbers, shredded lettuce and red onions were held at unsafe cold temperatures. The prep top cooler had insufficient holding capacity, requiring ice containers to be placed inside. The walk-in cooler had inadequate lighting, requiring the inspector to use a flashlight. The handwashing sink in the south restroom had inadequate water pressure, running only at a trickle. Dried food debris and ice built up on the walls and bottom of the reach-in freezer. Required temperature logs were unavailable for stored, thawed and cooked food items. The facility lacked calibration logs for its temperature-measuring devices.

headline: Five businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: 66 Diner
notes: Caked-on food debris and black matter accumulated on the prep kitchen ice machine shield, slicer and can opener blade. Employee liquid skin was stored improperly on prep kitchen food storage racks next to food thermometers. Frozen fish and green chile were thawed improperly in 80-degree standing water at the three-compartment sink. Rodent droppings and a rodent were found in a cabinet under the milkshake counter, alongside a live cockroach in the dining room. Soiled wiping cloths and a chemical spray bottle were stored on a wire rack directly above an open bag of onions. The person in charge failed to demonstrate food safety knowledge or prevent employee cross-contamination practices. The handwashing sink near the three-compartment sink provided hot water at only 80 degrees to 81 degrees. Unsealed structural gaps along an exterior CO2 port allowed potential pest entry into the facility. Chopped green chile and cooked sausages were stored outside cold holding on top of a cook line drawer unit. A box of cereal was left directly on the floor, and cooling ice wands were stored unprotected. The cookline handwashing sink was dirty, blocked by a trash can and improperly used as a water source for steam wells. Employees wore unapproved wrist jewelry, lacked hair restraints and stored personal drinks on prep-kitchen food shelving. Food handlers failed to wash their hands when changing gloves, switching tasks, or touching their face and body. An employee touched raw burger patties and then immediately handled a ready-to-eat burrito and lettuce garnish using the same gloved hands. Heavy grease and debris accumulated on walls and floors throughout the kitchen, bakery, walk-in cooler and dishwashing areas. The menu did not have the required consumer advisory reminder statement regarding raw or undercooked animal products, only a disclosure. Food scoops were stored with handles touching ingredients, food pans were stacked wet, and boxes were stored directly on the ground. Nonfood contact surfaces including equipment sides, cabinet interiors, walk-in fan shrouds and shelves had significant debris buildup. Kitchen, bakery and warewashing walls were in disrepair, with numerous holes, gaps and cracks.

entries.name: El Ranchito Meat Market
notes: Red and green chile in the display case lacked required common name labels. The establishment did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Nonfunctional and unused items like toys, tires, tools, car parts and appliances cluttered the back storage room and disused restrooms. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. Self-service slushie equipment near the cashier area lacked utensils or dispensing protection to prevent contamination. The handwashing sink in the meat department was in disrepair due to a plumbing disconnect at the sink basin. The facility lacked required temperature logs for stored and received raw meats and dairy products. No calibration logs were maintained for temperature-measuring devices. Raw meat inside the walk-in freezer was stored uncovered and unprotected from contamination. The food establishment permit was not posted on the premises. A meat slicer stored behind the meat display case was put away with food debris. Knives stored on the knife rack were put away soiled with raw meat debris. The facility failed to provide a designated area for employee dining or drinking. Handwashing sinks in the meat department and employee restroom lacked approved hand-drying provisions. Employee Gatorade bottles and soda cans were stored improperly on cutting boards and prep tables.

entries.name: Joe’s Pasta House
notes: Chlorine sanitizer concentration in the dish machine measured at zero ppm. Debris and slime accumulated inside the ice machine, and dried food debris built up on the can opener blade. Detergent was not dispensing from the dish machine because the chemical container was empty. An employee touched ready-to-eat bread with bare hands at the server station. The dish machine drain pipe was misaligned with the floor drain, causing water to spill onto the floor. A handwashing sink in the server area was used improperly to dump and melt ice. Lighting in the warewashing area was inadequate. A kitchen line employee prepared food without proper facial hair restraints. An employee put on new gloves without washing their hands first. Soil buildup and debris accumulated on floors underneath equipment and prep tables.

entries.name: KFC
notes: A dozen dead cockroaches were allowed to accumulate in the kitchen area and dining room. Prepared coleslaw and pot pies stored in the walk-in cooler lacked required date markings. Floor drains under the front counter and near the drive-through window had inadequate air gaps. Exterior front doors on the east side had small holes and gaps along the bottom that let light through. Food service pans in the warewashing area were wet-stacked instead of being allowed to air dry. Nonfood contact surfaces including soda machine backplates, dining furniture, windows, sink sides and kitchen pipes had heavy debris and grease buildup.

entries.name: Lindo Mexico
notes: Quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution in a wiping-cloth bucket on the cook line measured at zero ppm. Yellow slime built up inside the ice machine bin, and dried food debris accumulated on the can opener blade. Soiled wiping cloths were stored improperly on cutting boards and prep tables. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not have required food handler cards. Working containers of sugar and salt in dry storage and service areas lacked proper common name labels. The female restroom lacked a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. Employee drinks were stored on prep tables and coolers directly above open food items. The establishment was operating with an expired food permit. A food employee switched tasks and donned new gloves without washing their hands first. Chef knives were stored improperly inside pans of lettuce on the main cook line. Pans in the warewashing area were wet-stacked instead of being allowed to air dry.

entries.name: Dragon Sushi
notes: Unlabeled chlorine sanitizer was stored directly on the floor in the sushi bar area. The facility lacked documentation or evidence of routine pest control procedures. Cooked meats, tempura shrimp, fried vegetables and imitation crab were held at room temperature below 135 degrees. Over-the-counter Raid pesticide was present in the sushi preparation area. Sliced vegetables stored in the walk-in refrigerator lacked date markings. The person in charge failed to demonstrate required food safety knowledge. The three-compartment sink faucet was in disrepair and could not shut off completely. A bulk container of flour in the kitchen lacked a common name label. Raw eggs were stored directly above fresh produce in the walk-in refrigerator. Garage doors remained wide open during operations, and the front entrance door was not self-closing. Raw fish and seafood in the sushi bar were held at unsafe cold temperatures up to 54 degrees. Food probe thermometers were not provided, and cold-holding units lacked ambient measuring devices. The facility failed to provide a designated break area for employees. The main kitchen handwashing sink was blocked by a Gatorade bottle inside the basin. Chlorine sanitizer solution in a bucket exceeded maximum allowable concentration at over 200 ppm. An employee kept an unapproved twist-top Gatorade bottle in food preparation areas. The food establishment permit was not posted on the premises. Floor and wall surfaces in the kitchen and sushi bar area were not smooth or easily cleanable.

entries.name: Panera Bread
notes: The warewashing machine failed to sanitize utensils, organic growth built up inside the ice machine and a blender was left soaking in dirty sink water. Live cockroaches were present in the dining room and beverage station area. Dead cockroaches accumulated on the floor in the mop sink and bakery areas. Damaged wood composite shelving in the beverage and bakery areas was in disrepair and improperly used as a cutting board. The warewashing machine operated below required temperatures at 84 degrees and 97 degrees. Outdoor waste bins were left open and uncovered. The person in charge failed to demonstrate required food safety knowledge or maintain sanitary facility conditions. Self-service beverage bar dairy exceeded allowable time limits while held outside temperature control. Plumbing under dump sinks, the three-compartment sink, beverage stations, mop sink, and water heater leaked water onto floors and inside cabinets. Kitchen sinks lacked required backflow prevention air gaps. Food employees did not have required food handler cards. Ventilation ducts and a pedestal fan shroud had heavy debris buildup. Exterior doors were not tight-fitting, allowing light through the edges. A cardboard box of melons was stored directly on the floor in the walk-in cooler. A toilet fixture in the men’s restroom had significant soil residue buildup. An employee wore unapproved wrist jewelry while preparing open food items. Food employees worked on the kitchen line and bakery area without proper hair restraints. A line cook wiped down prep boards and donned gloves without washing hands first. Soil buildup and debris accumulated on walls and floors throughout the kitchen, prep and warewashing areas. Food service pans were stacked wet in the warewashing area. Nonfood contact surfaces on equipment sides, shelving and cabinets had significant debris accumulation. Walls in the back area, drive-thru and prep areas were in disrepair, with holes, gaps and cracks.

entries.name: Presbyterian
notes: Debris accumulated on the ice machine ice chute and can opener blade. Minimal rodent droppings were found along a pillar near the steam kettles. Sliced meat in juice, chicken strips and potato wedges were held at unsafe hot temperatures between 110 degrees and 126 degrees. Soiled wiping cloths were stored on prep tables and draped over sanitizer bucket edges. Open bulk tubs of hummus and jelly in a pitcher lacked required date markings. A hot-holding unit door gasket was torn and dangling, and the can opener blade had visible damage. Plumbing at the prep sink, equipment piping and dish area leaked water onto the floor. Prep sinks and washing sinks lacked required backflow prevention air gaps. Working containers of bulk dried spices lacked common name labels. Hummus and grape jelly were held at unsafe cold temperatures of 45 degrees and 46 degrees in a reach-in cooler. An employee handled soiled patient dishes and then handled clean utensils without washing hands first. Buildup and debris accumulated on walls, floors and refrigerator shelving throughout the kitchen. Assorted pans and food containers were wet-stacked on drying racks instead of air drying. Nonfood contact surfaces on equipment, ovens, vents, hot-holding unit interiors and caster wheels had heavy debris buildup. Kitchen walls and floors were in disrepair with numerous gaps, holes, cracks, and crevices. Kitchen floor surfaces made of poorly repaired concrete and eroded tile grout were not smooth or easily cleanable.

entries.name: Royal Buffet Restaurant
notes: A stainless steel lid was washed improperly in a prep sink next to thawing raw baby octopus. Six chemical spray bottles containing degreaser, ortho concentrates and unknown liquids lacked common-name labels. Hot foods in the self-service buffet steam table were double-panned, preventing adequate hot-holding capacity. Canned food items in the dry storage area were dented on and around their seams. Shredded crab meat and sushi rolls in the sushi area were held at unsafe temperatures of 72 degrees and 60 degrees. The sushi display cooler had a broken glass door missing a large piece, allowing cold air to escape. Probe food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible.

entries.name: Sonic Drive-In
notes: Yellow and brown soil residue built up inside the ice machine bin, and dried food debris accumulated on the food dicer, tomato slicer and food service pans. Spray bottles of degreaser were stored on a prep table on top of Ziploc bags and next to utensils at the front three-compartment sink. Prepared burger patties stored in the walk-in and upright coolers lacked required date markings. An ice scoop was stored inside a wall holder filled with stagnant water near the ice machine. Plumbing pipes under the three-compartment sink leaked grey water directly onto the floor. Interior ventilation intake and exhaust ducts in the kitchen and restrooms had debris buildup. Raw burger patties were stored directly above ready-to-eat red chile in an upright cooler. Exterior doors were not tight-fitting, and the back door was propped open. Kitchen handwashing sinks had soil debris buildup, and paper towel dispensers were covered in heavy dust. Lighting inside the walk-in cooler was inadequate. A kitchen food employee handled open food items without proper hair restraints. Substantial soil debris and grease accumulated on floors, walls and ceilings throughout the facility. Single-use drinking cups and portion cups were stored directly on the floor in the storage area outside the back door. Nonfood contact surfaces across all equipment, shelving, prep tables, and sinks had heavy grease and food buildup.

entries.name: Spicy Junction
notes: Chlorine sanitizer in a sanitizing bucket was below the required concentration at less than 50 ppm at 88 degrees. A standing mixer and stainless-steel containers were stored in the clean dish area with food debris buildup. Multiple spray bottles containing chlorine sanitizer and concentrated bleach lacked common name labels. Hot white rice at 111 degrees was cooled improperly inside a prep unit, and the kitchen lacked adequate equipment to cool large stock pots of cooked beef. Food employees did not have required food handler cards or approved food safety training. A working container of flour stored on prep table shelving lacked a common name label. Foil used to line a spice rack shelf and cold-holding unit interior was not smooth or easily cleanable. The female restroom lacked a covered trash receptacle for sanitary napkins. Unused equipment and cluttered miscellaneous items, including a nonfunctional small refrigerator, accumulated near the cashier area. Multiple cold-held foods in prep and standing coolers were held at unsafe temperatures ranging from 46 degrees to 111 degrees. The facility lacked designated storage facilities for employee personal items, with eyeglasses found stored above a microwave. The food establishment permit was not posted on the premises. Purchase stickers remained on beverage glasses stored on clean dish shelving.

entries.name: Stuffed Lust Sopapilla Co.
notes: Potentially hazardous foods in standing cold-holding and prep units — including red chile, cooked meats, beans, rice, cheese and vegetables — were held at unsafe temperatures between 45 degrees and 65 degrees. The cold-holding prep table was nonoperational and frozen over, failing to maintain safe cold-holding temperatures. The three-compartment sink lacked sufficient hot water and failed to reach 110 degrees.

entries.name: Taco Cabana
notes: Brown and yellow organic growth built up inside the ice machine near the tortilla machine. Spray bottles containing degreaser lacked required common name labels. An electrocution insect control device was installed directly over a food preparation area on the main cook line. Prepared beef and chicken flautas stored in the walk-in cooler lacked required date markings. An employee touched ready-to-eat rice with bare hands while moving it to a food container. Chile rellenos and shredded cheese in prep coolers on the main cook line were held at unsafe temperatures of 51 degrees and 54 degrees. The handwashing sink in the men’s restroom lacked required handwashing signage. Employees failed to wash hands when changing tasks and gloves, including transitioning from dishwashing to food preparation. Substantial soil buildup and debris accumulated on floors under equipment and inside floor drains, particularly near the lobby soda machine. The facility failed to provide written allergen notifications for unpackaged foods served to consumers. Food service pans in the warewashing area were stacked wet without air drying. Nonfood contact surfaces — including walk-in cooler fan shrouds, ice bin lids, and the soda machine backplate — had food and soil debris buildup.

headline: 13 businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Curry Leaf
notes: A knife, a vegetable dicer and a Robot Coupe were stored with food debris buildup. Glass cleaner and eyeglass cleaner were stored inside soup bowls on the clean dish storage rack. Carrot mix, cooked meat and green paste failed to maintain hot-holding temperatures. Employees improperly cleaned up rodent droppings by wiping off a food storage container in the kitchen back prep area. Prepared vegetables, soups and sauces stored in standing reach-in refrigerators lacked required date markings. Cutting boards on cold-prep units had deep scratches and scoring. The person in charge failed to demonstrate food safety knowledge due to multiple priority violations. Main kitchen hood filters were damaged, leaving substantial gaps and grease/debris buildup. Plastic food containers holding ingredients removed from original packaging were stored in a tub without common-name labels. Cold-held items failed to maintain safe temperatures, including green chile, raw shrimp and shredded cheese. The facility lacked lockers or designated areas for employee clothing and personal belongings. An employee wore an unapproved wristwatch while preparing raw chicken and entrees. Multiple employees prepared food along the main kitchen line without hair restraints. Debris and rodent droppings were observed underneath shelving and prep tables in the back kitchen area. A substantial number of rodent droppings were found on wooden shelving in the back prep area. The establishment failed to maintain required temperature logs for stored, cooled or received temperature-controlled foods.

entries.name: Dave’s High Desert Grill
notes: Yellow buildup was found inside the ice machine, and dried food debris was present on chef knives and a food wedger. Soiled wiping cloths were stored on prep tables and cutting boards. Four quarts of pooled eggs were left on the cook line counter without being prepared for an immediate order or batter. Multiple prepared items in reach-in coolers lacked date markings, including cooked meats, cut vegetables and sauces. The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Raw eggs were stored directly over ready-to-eat cheeses, sliced onions and corn. Cold-held items failed to maintain safe temperatures, including pooled eggs, diced tomatoes and shredded cheese. Multiple food items were left out on the prep table counter without ice or refrigeration. Restroom handwashing sinks lacked required handwashing signage. A handwashing sink near the main cook line was improperly used as a dump sink for blueberries. An employee wore a wristwatch and bracelets while working with open food. Food service pans were stacked wet in the washing area. The facility failed to maintain required temperature logs for stored foods. No calibration logs were available for temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Eat My Thai Cuisine
notes: Standing reach-in coolers and prep tables failed to maintain safe cold-holding temperatures.

entries.name: Federico’s
notes: Frozen fish was improperly thawing in ambient air in the kitchen. Prepared items in make tables and reach-in coolers lacked date markings, including salsas, prepared meats and diced vegetables. The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Cold-held items in the refrigerated make table and upright cooler failed to maintain safe temperatures, including shrimp, sausage and guacamole. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. The facility failed to maintain required temperature logs for hot and cold temperature-controlled foods.

entries.name: Kap’s
notes: Clean linens were found sitting in standing water. No sanitizer was prepared or available at the front service counter. Black organic matter was present near the ice chute of the ice machine. An unlabeled plastic spray bottle containing an unknown chemical liquid was stored in the facility. A live cockroach was observed next to cooking equipment near a crack in the wall. Dozens of dead roaches accumulated under equipment, and a dead mouse was left in a trap under the soda machine. Two dozen pooled eggs were stored in a reach-in cooler without being prepared for an immediate customer order or batter. Prepared green chile exceeded the seven-day storage limit, and raw chicken was left unlabeled. The person in charge failed to demonstrate required food safety knowledge. A floor drain near the cook line was in disrepair with standing water. Kitchen line ventilation fins had bird feathers stuck to them, and the exterior exhaust duct was dirty. A ripped Styrofoam package of mushrooms was stored in the walk-in cooler. Raw chicken was stored directly next to mushrooms in the line reach-in cooler. The restroom lacked a tight-fitting, self-closing door. A hole was present in the wall by the dish pit. Temperature-measuring devices for thin foods were not provided or accessible. Chlorine sanitizer in a container exceeded the maximum permitted concentration level. The dry storage area lacked lighting entirely. An employee wore an unapproved wristwatch while preparing food. A kitchen line employee failed to wear a hat or beard guard. A soiled mop was stored directly on the floor. Extreme grease and food debris buildup was observed on kitchen walls, floors and equipment. Facility walls were in disrepair with holes near the dish pit and throughout the kitchen.

entries.name: Kinder Care Learning Center
