Working spray bottles containing unknown bulk liquid were not labeled. TCS foods in hot holding, including chile rellenos, green chile sauce and red chile, measured below safe temperatures. Wiping cloths used for sanitizing kitchen line countertops were stored on the counter instead of in sanitizer solution. Ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in and prep top coolers exceeded the seven-day storage limit. An inadequate air gap was provided at the floor drain under the warewashing machine. Food employees did not have valid food handler cards. Air vents and exhaust ducts in the kitchen area had debris buildup. Food service bins holding sugar and flour in dry storage were not labeled with common names. The female employee restroom lacked a covered trash receptacle for sanitary napkins. The rear exterior door was not tight-fitting and allowed light through the edges. TCS foods in the main cook line prep cooler, including shredded cheese, diced tomatoes, pico de gallo and shredded lettuce, measured at unsafe cold-holding temperatures. The facility lacked a designated area for employees to eat, drink or use tobacco products. Hot water at employee restroom handwashing sinks was insufficient, reaching only 75 degrees. Buildup and debris accumulated on the floor under the upright cooler near the sopapilla station. Written notifications of major food allergens were missing for unpackaged foods. A cooking pot was used as a scoop and stored inside food with its handle directly touching the product. Food service pans in the warewashing area were wet-stacked without air drying. Temperature logs were not maintained for stored TCS foods. Calibration logs were not maintained for temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Freska King
notes: Debris buildup was present on the exterior of reach-in coolers and inside cooler vent covers. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or accessible for measuring thin foods. Chemical sanitizer testing devices and chlorine test strips were not available. A reach-in cooler measured at 55 degrees and lacked sufficient capacity to keep food cold. Cleanser was missing at the handwashing sink. A handwashing sign was not provided at the handwashing sink. Temperature logs were missing for milk cold-holding and cooler ambient air temperatures. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained. Thermometers scaled for both celsius and fahrenheit were missing from reach-in coolers. Water pressure at the handwashing sink was inadequate, with water barely coming out of the faucet.

entries.name: Olympia Cafe
notes: Facility is subject to a follow-up inspection five days after reopening.

entries.name: Quesadilla Way
notes: Facility is subject to a follow-up inspection five days after reopening.

entries.name: Sergio’s Bakery & Cafe
notes: A meat slicer stored away above a prep table had substantial food debris buildup. TCS foods in hot-holding, including marinara, meatballs and display pizzas, failed the required temperature standards. Pooled eggs measuring 52 degrees were held inside a cold-holding unit. Ready-to-eat TCS foods inside a cold-holding unit lacked required date markings. Green chile sauce at 115 degrees was cooling improperly inside a cold-holding unit while covered. Hood vent filters and ventilation ducts inside the main kitchen had grease and debris buildup. TCS foods in the front pizza prep cold-holding unit measured at unsafe temperatures. A designated area was not provided for employee eating or personal belongings. A food employee preparing pizzas in the kitchen lacked proper hair restraints. The facility operated with an expired permit. An employee touched a cellphone with gloved hands, placed hands in pockets, wiped gloves on an apron and resumed food preparation without washing hands. Stainless steel kitchen shelving had soil residue buildup. Required temperature logs for stored, received and cooled TCS foods were not available.

entries.name: Shalom Assisted Living
notes: Chemical sanitizing solution in a spray bottle failed to meet required parameters, testing at 0ppm. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees were not in possession of valid food handler cards or approved training records. Working containers of sugar and flour inside kitchen cabinets were not labeled with common food names. Nonfood-contact surfaces inside kitchen cabinets were made of damaged synthetic wood that was not smooth. The restroom was not equipped with a tight-fitting, self-closing door. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. Handwashing cleanser was missing at handwashing sinks in the kitchen and employee restroom. Hot water was unavailable at the kitchen handwashing sink because the hot water knob was nonfunctional. A food employee was observed washing hands in a three-compartment sink instead of a designated handwashing sink.

entries.name: Stripes Burrito Co.
notes: Yellow buildup was observed inside the ice machine. Chicken tenders in hot-holding failed to meet required temperature standards. Approximately 90 quarts of pooled raw eggs were stored in the walk-in cooler. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts throughout the kitchen area had debris buildup. TCS foods in the walk-in cooler, including raw chicken, carne adovada, onions, barbacoa, potatoes, milk, pooled eggs, raw pork and salsa, measured at unsafe cold-holding temperatures An employee actively working with open food items wore unapproved wrist jewelry and gemmed rings. A food employee actively working with open food on the main cook line lacked proper hair restraints. Written notifications of major food allergens were missing for unpackaged foods. Soil debris buildup was present on the spray faucet for the three-compartment sink. The kitchen ceiling was in disrepair with a large hole cut into it for repair work. Temperature logs were not maintained for stored TCS foods. Calibration logs were not maintained for temperature-measuring devices.

entries.name: Sushi Freak
notes: Chlorine sanitizer in the automatic dish machine and quaternary sanitizer in red wiping buckets tested at 0 ppm. Ready-to-eat TCS foods in the walk-in refrigerator, including sauces, cucumbers, onion rings, seaweed, fish eggs and coleslaw mix, lacked required date markings. The person in charge failed to demonstrate required knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, food safety temperatures or proper sanitizer concentrations. The toilet inside the men’s restroom was in disrepair and constantly running and flushing repeatedly. Inadequate air gaps were provided at the three-compartment sink, soda machine floor drain and main kitchen line floor drain. Vinegar was added to white rice as a method of preservation without an approved variance. TCS foods on the cold-holding make table, including cooked shrimp, raw fish, tuna mix, coleslaw mix, sliced cucumbers and chopped green chile, were measured at unsafe temperatures. Lockers or suitable facilities were not provided for storing employee personal belongings. Thermometers were missing from the cold-holding unit. Buildup and debris accumulated underneath cold-holding units, behind the cooktop and on kitchen shelving. Stainless steel cabinets had substantial food debris buildup on interior nonfood-contact surfaces.

entries.name: The Melting Pot
notes: Quaternary sanitizer in red buckets and the three-compartment sink tested at 0 ppm. A vegetable dicer was stored away with food debris buildup, and a vaping device was placed on a cutting board in the food prep area. Working spray bottles containing chemical sanitizer were not labeled with common names. An estimated 40 to 50 living and dead cockroaches accumulated on glue boards in closets, along dishware shelving and under a soda table. The facility lacked adequate documentation and procedures to effectively control pests. Substantial rodent droppings were found underneath clutter and shelving in the back storage room. Ready-to-eat TCS foods, including prepared potatoes, corn on the cob, sauces and vegetarian balls, lacked required date markings. The person in charge failed to demonstrate required knowledge of sanitizer concentrations, foodborne illnesses or prevent priority violations. The men’s handwashing sink could not completely shut off, and kitchen floor drains had food debris buildup and dead cockroaches. An inadequate air gap was provided underneath the three-compartment sink leading to the floor drain. Food employees did not have valid food handler cards. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts above the kitchen make line had debris buildup. A working container holding flour or starch in the back storage area was not labeled with its common name. Unused, nonfunctional items, including electronics, decor, bikes, tools and shop vacs, cluttered storage and service areas. TCS foods on the salad make line, including boiled eggs, dressing, bleu cheese, and salsa, were measured at unsafe cold temperatures. Chemical sanitizing solution test kits were not available. Designated areas were not provided for employee eating, drinking or personal belongings. Thermometers were missing from the walk-in refrigerator and cold-holding units. Buildup and debris accumulated underneath cold-holding units, the ice machine, the automatic dish machine, prep tables and storage shelving. Floor and wall juncture coving had substantial gaps and holes underneath the three-compartment sink and automatic dish machine. Temperature logs for stored and received TCS foods were not maintained. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

headline: Thirteen businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Applebee’s
notes: The facility was conveying sewage, posing an imminent health hazard. The interior chute of the ice machine in the back prep area had black soil residue. Three units of cooked diced chicken in the walk-in cooler were held past their expiration date. Hand wash, prep and mop sinks were leaking and dripping. Cold-holding equipment in the grill drawers failed to maintain safe temperatures for stored foods. The handwashing sink in the cooking area lacked an approved hand-drying provision. Direct connections existed between the sewage system and food equipment drains in the back prep and freezer areas. Stainless steel cooking and refrigeration equipment had dry food debris and soil buildup on non-food contact surfaces. Floors and drains in the food prep and storage areas had debris buildup. Quarry tile floors and base coving in the cook and prep areas were damaged, cracked or missing.

entries.name: Clyde Hotel Carrie’s
notes: Heavy rodent droppings were present along the kitchen line, inside broken equipment, in the service area and in the dining room, with no control methods in place. Sanitizer in a bucket failed to meet required concentration levels, measuring at 100 PPM. The interior ceiling and ice chute of the ice machine had heavy soil and debris buildup. Ready-to-eat foods in the prep top cooler were held past their expiration dates. Door gaskets on reach-in and prep top coolers were torn, and prep top cooler lids were broken with pieces hanging off. The person in charge failed to maintain active managerial control to prevent imminent health hazards and priority violations. Warewashing machine piping was leaking grey water into a bucket placed underneath. Plumbing fixtures, including faucets and pipes, were leaking water profusely. Inadequate air gaps were provided at prep sinks, single-basin sinks and three-compartment sinks throughout the kitchen. Multiple exterior doors were not tight-fitting, allowing light to show along the edges. Unused and nonfunctional equipment with accumulated debris and rodent droppings was stored in the kitchen and lobby areas. Employee personal belongings were stored on open shelving directly above cleaned and sanitized dishes. Heavy soil buildup and debris were present on walls and floors throughout the kitchen, service, warewashing and dining areas. No written notification of major food allergens was provided for unpackaged food. Menu items served raw or undercooked lacked adequate consumer advisory disclosures and reminders. Cleaned food pans were wet stacked in the storage area before air drying. Nonfood-contact surfaces, including equipment sides, equipment interiors and shelving compressor areas, had soil residue buildup. Walls throughout the storage, kitchen, service, and lobby areas had numerous gaps, cracks, holes and crevices.

entries.name: Clyde Hotel Mercantile
notes: Sanitizer solution in buckets failed to meet required concentration levels, measuring at 0 PPM. A working plastic squeeze bottle containing dish soap lacked a label identifying its common name. Multiple prepared ready-to-eat foods in the display cooler, including parfaits, salads and quiche, lacked date markings. The person in charge failed to maintain active managerial control to prevent an imminent health hazard and priority violations. The floor drain located under the counter area was missing a strainer. The counter near the cash register area had an inadequate air gap. An employee preparing sandwiches was observed wearing unapproved wrist jewelry. A food employee failed to wash hands when switching tasks and donning new gloves. A soiled mop was stored directly on the floor instead of being positioned to air dry. Packaged foods in display cases lacked required labeling information, including ingredients and major food allergens.

entries.name: Clyde Hotel Banquet Kitchen
notes: The Environmental Health Department conducted an in-person walkthrough of The Clyde Hotel Banquet Kitchen and has upgraded it to unsatisfactory status.

entries.name: Helen’s Bakery
notes: Facility is being reopened under an unsatisfactory status. It will remain in that status for five business days.

entries.name: Keller’s Farm Store
notes: Temperature logs were not available for stored TCS foods. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained. An employee at the deli station washed hands for only 5-7 seconds and used a bare hand to turn off the faucet. Light bulbs in the walk-in cooler lacked protective shielding or shatter-resistant covers. A can opener blade stored in a cabinet had dried food debris buildup. Approved hand-drying provisions were missing at all handwashing sinks throughout the facility. Handwashing signage was missing at employee restroom handwashing sinks. Multiple prepared ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in cooler, including hard-boiled eggs, cooked potatoes, cooked bacon bits and an unknown sauce, lacked date markings. Ready-to-eat foods, including milk, roast mix, hocks, pork hocks and sliced tomatoes, were held past the seven-day limit.

entries.name: Mom’s Cafe
notes: Multiple prepared ready-to-eat foods in the retail cooler, reach-in cooler, and cold-holding table, including pasta salad, macaroni salad, diced tomatoes, red chile and green chile, lacked date markings. The facility did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Food temperature-measuring devices suitable for measuring thin foods were not provided or readily accessible. No testing kits or devices were available to measure chemical sanitizing concentrations. The facility was operating with an expired permit. An electrical cover behind cooking equipment was missing, and a hole in the ceiling lacked a vent cover. Temperature logs for hot holding, cold holding, and equipment were not maintained for TCS foods. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

entries.name: Morada Quintessence
notes: Ice machines in the kitchen dry storage and dining room had organic substance buildup inside the bins. A can opener blade in the kitchen had dried food debris buildup. Drain pipes under the three-compartment sink and warewashing machine were leaking grey water directly onto the floor. Inadequate air gaps were provided at floor drains under the prep sink and warewashing area. The facility did not have a certified food protection manager on staff. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts in the kitchen area had debris buildup. Untreated wood shelving in server closets and cabinets was absorbent and not easily cleanable. TCS foods, including cooked chicken, V8 juice and milk, were held above 41 degrees. A designated employee break area was not provided, and an employee drink was stored in the walk-in cooler directly above food. Walk-in cooler flooring had dried blood under raw meat, and the floor under the warewashing machine had substantial food buildup. In-use scoops and cups in the main kitchen area were stored inside food containers with handles directly touching the food.

entries.name: Sonic Drive-In
notes: Food-contact equipment, including the ice machine, hot dog roller, ladles, scoops, trays and ice cream blenders, was heavily soiled with food residue, grease and organic matter. Prepared ready-to-eat foods in the reach-in cooler, including sliced onions, prepped tomatoes and ranch sauce, lacked date markings. The reach-in cooler under the prep table was not maintained in good repair and contained a heavy amount of standing water where food was stored. The person in charge failed to demonstrate basic food safety knowledge and foodborne disease prevention. TCS foods on the prep table, including sliced cheese and shredded cheese, were held above 41 degrees. Multiple food employees failed to wash hands when switching tasks. Heavy liquid wastewater accumulated on kitchen floors and was tracked through the food preparation area. Floors and walls throughout the kitchen, particularly under food equipment, had debris and soil buildup. Nonfood-contact surfaces on reach-in coolers, steam tables and beverage/ice cream stations had excessive food residue and soil accumulation. Consistent temperature logs were not maintained for stored, thawed or cooled TCS foods.

notes: This follow-up inspection is the result of a complaint received by the city.

Nonfood-contact surfaces, including light covers, ice machine exteriors and walk-in cooler vent covers, had debris buildup. Temperature logs for cold holding, hot holding, cooling, and equipment were not maintained. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

Employee personal items, including a headphone case, keys and sunglasses, were not stored in designated lockers or storage facilities. The handwashing sink on the east side of the kitchen was blocked and inaccessible due to a speed rack filled with pizzas. Quaternary ammonium sanitizer in a bucket exceeded maximum concentration limits, measuring over 400 PPM. Multiple kitchen employees handling open TCS foods were without proper hair restraints. Heavy buildup and debris were present on the floor drains. An in-use cup without a handle was stored directly inside a container of cheese.

entries.name: Little Caesars
notes: Ready-to-eat TCS foods under the cold-holding unit — including cubed ham, chopped green chile, cooked sausage, sliced pepperoni, and chopped vegetables — lacked date markings. entries.name: Quick Track
notes: Ready-to-eat TCS foods in the undercounter cooler — including shredded cheese and cooked chicken wings — exceeded the seven-day holding limit. The floor drain under the three-compartment sink was missing a strainer. The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards or approved food safety training. No testing kit or device was available to measure the concentration of chemical sanitizing solution. No approved hand-drying method was available at the back-of-house handwashing sink. The back-of-house handwashing sink was improperly used to store plastic food containers.

entries.name: Quick Track
notes: The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards or approved food safety training. Inadequate water pressure was observed at handwashing sinks, with hot water flowing at a trickle. Hot water was insufficient throughout the facility, reaching only 75 degrees at handwashing sinks, and was turned off at the three-compartment sink and mop sink. Raw eggs were stored above and leaking onto containers of half-and-half in the retail cooler. The ceiling was in disrepair, leaking rainwater into buckets and trash cans throughout the facility. Temperature logs were not maintained for stored TCS food items at the Hunts Bros. Pizza station. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained. Dead cockroaches accumulated near the ATM and back sink area. Dried food debris was present on a food dicer, pizza cutter and spatula at the Hunts Bros. Pizza station. Handwashing signage was missing at the Hunts Bros. Pizza handwashing sink. The Hunts Bros. Pizza handwashing sink was improperly used with a coffee cup in the basin.

headline: Eight businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Japanese Kitchen
notes: Chlorine sanitizing solution in the automatic dish machine measured at 0 PPM. A working spray bottle containing bulk disinfectant was not labeled with its common name. Ready-to-eat TCS foods in reach-in and walk-in refrigerators — including chopped green onion, sliced onion, mixed vegetables and imitation crab meat — lacked required date markings. A cutting board on the main cook line had deep scratches and scoring that prevented effective cleaning and sanitizing. The facility lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Food temperature-measuring devices were not provided or readily accessible. Lockers or suitable storage areas were not provided for employee clothing or personal belongings. Lighting was inadequate on the main cook line hood vent suppression system because no lights were installed. Single-use frozen seaweed and calamari salad containers were improperly reused for cold holding storage.

entries.name: Rising Star Chinese Eatery
notes: Chlorine sanitizing solution in wiping cloth containers measured at 0 PPM. Staff rinsed a stainless steel bowl used for raw beef and placed it on shelving without properly cleaning and sanitizing it. Cooling TCS foods — breaded fried chicken — failed to cool to 70 degrees within two hours. The hood ventilation system did not adequately collect grease and condensation, allowing drips onto the wall behind the wok and fryer station. Raw frozen shrimp was improperly thawing in a three-compartment sink basin while an employee pre-washed dishes in the adjacent basins. Tissue was not available at a toilet in the men’s restroom. Pot stickers stored in the bottom area of a prep top cooler failed to maintain safe cold-holding temperatures, measuring at 75 degrees. Accumulations of grease and debris were present on floors, walls, prep table shelves, exterior cooler and freezer surfaces, and in the warewashing area. An in-use ice scoop was stored improperly inside the ice bin with its handle touching the ice. A container of cut raw onions was stored underneath a leaking or condensing drain line directly on top of warewashing machine chemicals.

entries.name: Starry Moon
notes: Excessive soil buildup and rust coated the interior ceiling of the ice machine. Mice droppings accumulated behind prep tables, sinks and the grease trap with no pest-control methods in place. Staff stored ready-to-eat TCS foods — including cut melons, strawberries, blueberries, oranges and pineapples — in the refrigerator without date markings. Food employees failed to provide valid food handler cards or proof of approved food safety training. Structural holes and gaps in the mop station, water heater area and hallway allowed potential pest entry. The front prep-top cooler failed to maintain adequate cold-holding temperatures, running at an ambient temperature of 89.9 degrees. The facility provided no testing kit or device to measure chemical sanitizer concentrations. The back prep handwashing sink lacked hand cleanser and paper towels. Staff mixed chlorine sanitizer in a wiping-cloth container above permitted limits, exceeding 200 PPM. Unshielded light bulbs hung over exposed food, equipment and utensils in the back prep area. Soil buildup and debris accumulated on floors, walls, drains, and underneath tables and equipment. An employee stored an ice scoop directly on top of a dirty ice machine. Absorbent base coving and epoxy flooring prevented effective cleaning. The facility maintained no temperature logs for stored TCS foods, including milks, cream and cut fruits.

entries.name: Stripes
notes: Staff mixed quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution in the front bucket below effective parameters, measuring 100 PPM. Staff improperly pooled raw eggs in advance. Staff stored two squeeze bottles of crema in the prep top cooler without date markings. Staff left two pans of ready-to-eat chicharrónes uncovered beneath a prep table. Soil and hard water buildup coated handwashing fixtures in food prep areas. Debris and soil accumulated on kitchen walls, drains and floors beneath equipment and cooler shelving. Excessive soil buildup accumulated on nonfood-contact equipment throughout the kitchen, including prep tables, storage racks, refrigerators, fryers, the grill, cooler drawers, door gaskets, hoods and stove burners.

headline: Four businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Little Lobitos
notes: Soil and debris buildup was observed on a reach-in cooler and dry goods shelving. Dead cockroaches and mice droppings were present in the kitchen and stock areas without pest control methods in place. Ten dead cockroaches were allowed to accumulate in a trap near the backstock reach-in coolers. Mice droppings were found in the stock room and kitchen area. Plumbing lines below a sink were in disrepair and leaking water. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Canned goods and single-service items were stored improperly in an unclean location with debris falling on top of them. The kitchen, water heater room and stock areas were in disrepair with holes in the floors, walls and ceiling. The facility failed to maintain temperature logs for TCS foods. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

entries.name: Dunkin Donuts
notes: The quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution in the front bucket and three-compartment sink failed to meet requirements, testing at 0 PPM. A black soil residue was present inside the ice machine near the ice chute. Mr. Clean erasers were stored above food containers and service articles. Two live cockroaches were found in the storage area without pest control methods in place. The establishment was closed due to an imminent health hazard of insufficient refrigeration, with the main refrigerator holding cream cheese and sliced cheese at 49 degrees and a reach-in cooler holding milk at 55 degrees. Open ice cream and other food boxes were exposed to dripping water from the walk-in freezer units. Three plumbing drains were in disrepair and missing required baskets and covers. An inadequate air gap was present at the front counter discharge tubing, which almost touched the bottom of the drain. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. Lockers or suitable storage for employee clothing and personal belongings were not provided. The women’s restroom lacked hand paper towels, and hand soap was missing from both the women’s restroom and the front handwashing station. Buildup and debris were found under donut cases, storage shelving and walk-in cooler shelving. Clean single-service and single-use articles, including lids and cups, were improperly stored on the floor near the freezer entry. Required temperature logs for TCS foods, including eggs, sausage, bacon, cheese, cream cheese and milk, had not been updated since Sept. 29, 2026.

entries.name: Ojos Locos
notes: Quaternary ammonium sanitizer in red buckets failed to meet required parameters, testing at 200 PPM. The main kitchen line lacked a sanitizer bucket setup while producing food. The ice machine had debris buildup, and a cheese grater, vegetable dicer and vegetable slicer were stored away with food debris on them. The warewashing dish machine and washing racks had substantial debris buildup. Working spray bottles containing alleged degreaser were not labeled with common names. Raw meats were improperly thawing at room temperature in the three-compartment sink. Used wiping cloths were improperly stored on prep tables and the kitchen line. An inadequate air gap was present at the floor drain in the three-compartment sink area. The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager, as the manager’s certification had expired on Aug. 14, 2026. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards or approved food safety training. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts in the back prep area had debris buildup. TCS foods in the middle prep cold-holding unit — including grilled jalapeños, guacamole, chopped tomatoes, shredded cheese, chopped onion, pickled onion and pico de gallo — were held at unsafe temperatures ranging from 45 to 75 degrees. Food temperature-measuring devices, such as a probe thermometer, were not available. Ambient air thermometers were missing from the inside of cold-holding units. The facility lacked a designated area for employees to eat, drink or use tobacco products. A handwashing sign was missing at the main kitchen line handwashing sink. The back prep area handwashing sink was blocked and made inaccessible by stored bar mugs. A food employee on the main kitchen and prep lines lacked proper hair restraints while preparing food and entrees. A manager, a cook and two prep employees switched job duties and changed positions without washing their hands. A soiled mop not in use was improperly stored directly on the floor instead of air-drying. Buildup and debris accumulated underneath the fryer, dish machine area, prep tables, cold-holding units and ice machine. Multiple ceiling tiles were missing above the ice machines. Temperature logs for TCS foods were not maintained. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

headline: Three businesses red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Panda Express
notes: The quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution in the wiping cloth bucket tested at 0 ppm and 68 degrees. The ice machine in the back storage area had significant organic debris inside and on the deflector shield. Unapproved home-based pesticides were present in the establishment. Over 15 dead cockroaches were allowed to accumulate under the drive-thru beverage dispensing machine. A designated person in charge was present, but no manager was on duty. An inadequate air gap was present in the back plumbing systems, including at the prep sink. Food employees did not have valid food handler cards or approved food safety training. Exterior doors were not tight-fitting and allowed light through the edges. The waste storage area and enclosure were unclean, with waste spilled on lids and fecal matter in the corral area. A bulk rice bin in the prep area was left open with a soiled perforated pan directly above it, exposing the food to contamination. Testing kits for chemical sanitizing solutions were not available. Quaternary sanitizer in the three-compartment sink exceeded the maximum permitted concentration, testing at over 400 ppm. A grade sticker was not posted on the facility. Buildup and debris were found on walls under the three-compartment sink and on floors in the drive-thru and lobby beverage station. A portion scoop was improperly stored inside a prep top cooler with its handle in direct contact with the food. Various sizes of pans were wet-stacked in the warewashing area without air drying. Significant debris accumulated in the drive-thru and cooking areas, inside cabinets, on coolers and gaskets and at the wok station. Soda syrup spills, dead insects and a significant odor were found under the drive-thru beverage station, which was being used to store straws. Walls throughout the drive-thru, mop sink, warewashing and service line areas were in disrepair with numerous gaps, cracks, holes and crevices.

headline: One business red-tagged in city’s latest inspection report

author: Journal Staff Report

entries.name: Circle K
notes: An imminent health hazard was declared due to a mouse infestation in the grocery retail areas and the backroom area near the sink and wall corners. The front double doors were not tight-fitting and allowed light through the edges. The facility failed to maintain adequate pest control procedures or follow up on repairs recommended by their pest control technician on Oct. 3. Mice on the sales floor chewed through several candy items. Mice droppings were found under shelving, inside candy boxes, and in the backroom area on both sides of the three-compartment sinks. A 12x12 square hole in the hallway wall contained chewed-up insulation. Debris and soil buildup were observed on grocery, cooler and liquor shelving.

entries.name: Madcrema
notes: Chlorine sanitizer in the barista wiping cloth bucket failed to meet required parameters, testing at 0 PPM. The ice maker and pots in the kitchen and clean dish storage areas had soil accumulation and food debris. An unapproved pesticide was improperly stored in the dish pit. Over 10 dead cockroaches were allowed to accumulate in traps in the kitchen, dish pit and restroom. Unused, nonfunctional and dirty items, including plastic single-use packages, kitchen equipment, linens and shirts, cluttered the kitchen, dish pit and exterior. The facility lacked a designated area for employees to eat, drink or use tobacco products. Lockers or suitable facilities were not provided for storing employee clothing and personal belongings. A food employee actively handling open food items in production areas lacked proper hair restraints. A food employee failed to wash their hands after switching tasks and before putting on new gloves. Buildup and debris accumulated on the kitchen floors, especially under food equipment and storage racks. Written notifications of major food allergens were missing for unpackaged foods. Single-use items, including pastry clamshell containers, beverage bottle packaging and milk packaging bottles, were improperly reused throughout the kitchen and reach-in refrigerators. Required temperature logs were not maintained for any hot- and cold-holding TCS foods. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

entries.name: Marielena’s Bakery
notes: The establishment lacked a certified food protection manager on staff. The entire facility was in disrepair, featuring holes in the walls, ceiling and floors, along with missing ceiling and floor tiles. Debris buildup was observed on nonfood-contact surfaces in the front retail, back cooking and storage areas, including countertops, the tops of ovens and prep equipment. The three-compartment sink faucet was in disrepair and had been removed, leaving only a spray nozzle available for use. An inadequate air gap was present in the back prep area, where pipes for the three-compartment sink and handwashing sink extended directly into the floor drain. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained. Temperature logs for TCS foods and equipment were not available. Live and dead cockroaches, rodents, flies and mice droppings were found throughout the facility. Buildup and debris accumulated on the floors, walls and ceilings throughout the whole facility. The facility operated with an expired permit. No chlorine sanitizing solution was prepared or available while the facility was actively loading racks of cooked pastries. Heavy debris buildup accumulated on food-contact surfaces, including mixers, ovens, utensils, sheet pans, retail holding shelves, pans, cups and bowls.

entries.name: Sushi Xuan
notes: Dried food debris was built up on the blade of a mandolin slicer in the kitchen prep area. A toxic degreaser was improperly stored next to a rack of tempura-battered meat. A working spray bottle containing alleged degreaser lacked a label with its common name. Ready-to-eat TCS foods in the upright and prep-top coolers, including tempura chicken, tempura batter and vegetables, lacked required date markings. An inadequate air gap was present at the floor drain under the warewashing machine. Food employees did not possess valid food handler cards or approved food safety training. Interior intake and exhaust air ducts in the kitchen area had debris buildup. A severely dented can of pineapple was found in the dry storage area. Large food service bins of flour and sugar in the kitchen prep area were not labeled with their common names. Raw squid and raw meat scraps were improperly stored above ready-to-eat food items in the upright cooler next to the main cook line. TCS foods in the prep top cooler and on a shelf — including sliced zucchini and tempura chicken — measured at unsafe cold-holding temperatures. Raw chicken, soft shell crab and raw beef were stored improperly less than 6 inches off the floor in the walk-in freezer, walk-in cooler and kitchen. Lockers or suitable facilities were not provided for storing employee clothing and personal belongings. The handwashing sink in the main kitchen had debris buildup. Handwashing signs were missing from all handwashing sinks, including in the bathrooms. An employee actively working with open food items wore unapproved wrist jewelry. A food employee actively working with open food items on the main kitchen line and prep area lacked proper hair restraints. Hot water was turned off at the kitchen handwashing sink next to the main cook line. Fish intended for raw consumption, such as salmon at the sushi station, lacked parasite destruction documentation or verification from the supplier. An employee failed to wash their hands when required after changing tasks, touching their body, changing gloves, and returning to the kitchen. Employees were observed improperly washing their hands in the three-compartment sink and prep sink instead of designated handwashing sinks. Buildup and debris accumulated on the kitchen floors, walls and ceilings, with substantial debris under the wok station. Scoops and containers in dry storage bins were improperly stored with their handles and all sides touching the food product inside. Food service pans were wet-stacked in the warewashing area without air drying. Single-use to-go boxes, lids and cups were improperly stored directly on the floor in the suite next door. Heavy debris buildup was present on equipment, particularly on the sides of the fryers and the wok station. Temperature logs for stored TCS foods were not maintained. Calibration logs for temperature-measuring devices were not maintained.

entries.name: Whole Hog Cafe
notes: Shredded cheese in the walk-in cooler lacked proper date markings and was discarded. A prep cook failed to change their single-use gloves after cutting raw chicken and proceeded to touch beef with the same gloves. Cheese sauce was improperly cooled by being left covered at room temperature in the prep area. Chlorine sanitizer at the front counter exceeded the maximum permitted concentration, testing at 200 PPM. Light bulbs in a reach-in cooler holding potato salad and other ready-to-eat foods lacked protective shielding or shatter-proof covers. Hot water was unavailable at both handwashing sinks in the prep and on-line areas. A food employee failed to wash their hands when required after prepping food. The dish area was in disrepair with holes in the ceiling. Required temperature logs were not maintained for TCS foods, including potato salad, ribs, brisket, pulled pork and baked potatoes.
